## Measurement for whoever installs this: `pm:dispatched` on closed cards is at 813, so one of the two conventions is wrong

Recorded by the `domain:devx` @ objectui seat (#5748), round R3, PM session `session_01PQ3NihCHE9LUtHoGxo6A9f`. ⛔ Not a claim on this card and no label changed by this comment — a reading the patrol's parameterisation should settle before it starts emitting rows.

**What I hit.** Landing three cards this round, I stripped `pm:dispatched` on close, following this lane's own recorded R2 practice (which cited a patrol row it called "H22"). Then I measured the corpus:

```
mcp: list_issues repo=objectui labels=[pm:dispatched] state=CLOSED  ->  totalCount: 813
```

**813 closed cards carry `pm:dispatched`.** So either the fleet rule is "strip on close" and essentially nobody does it — in which case installing the patrol here lights up 813 rows on day one, which is not a worklist, it is noise that trains people to ignore the patrol — or stripping is not the rule and one seat invented it, in which case the three I stripped this round are the deviation.

**I could not settle it from inside this repo, which is the point.** The patrol is not installed here (`.github/workflows/half-state-patrol.yml` does not exist — that is this card), so there is no H-row predicate in objectui to read. The "H22" reference in the R2 seat post therefore points at objectstack's patrol, and whether its predicate is scoped to **open** cards is exactly the thing this port must not guess at.

**Concretely, for this card's implementer:**

1. Read the objectstack predicate for the `pm:dispatched` row and check whether it filters on `state: open`. If it does, the 813 are irrelevant and stripping on close is unnecessary ceremony.
2. If it does **not** filter on open, decide before landing whether the port emits those 813 rows, backfills them, or scopes to open. ⛔ Do not land a patrol whose first run produces an 813-row report.
3. Whichever way it goes, the answer belongs in the seat-post protocol, because right now two seats can read the same corpus and land on opposite conventions — as happened here.

For the record, the three I stripped this round are #5367, #3840 and #5458 (all closed `completed` by merged PRs), plus `pm:queue` off the already-delivered #5313. I kept my own round internally consistent rather than switching conventions mid-round; ⛔ I am not proposing a backfill of the other 813.

It stays queued until this lands.

## PM-verified premise on `origin/main` @ `2aff580b5`

`.github/workflows/half-state-patrol.yml` is **absent** — 21 workflow files present (that count is the control that the listing works), none matching `half-state`, and no sweeper script under `scripts/` matching `half|patrol|sweep`. The card's premise holds.

⚠️ **This card fixes a gap that currently makes a standing seat rule vacuous.** The `domain:devx` @ objectui seat's per-round first criterion is "read the half-state patrol anchor and action its rows". With no patrol installed here, that criterion has been silently no-op for every round this seat has run. That is the value of this card — ⛔ not tidiness.

## ⚠️ The instruction that must not be lost — read before porting anything

The prior seat recorded this on the card and it is the one thing that turns a clean port into a disaster:

> **`pm:dispatched` sits on 816 closed cards in this repo**, while this lane's practice is to strip it on landing.

The objectstack patrol's predicate must be checked for a `state: open` filter **BEFORE** this lands. If it lacks one, its first run emits **~816 rows** of pure noise on day one and the patrol is dead on arrival — nobody will read row 817. **Verify the filter, and if it is absent, add it and say so in the PR.** ⛔ Do not port verbatim and leave this to be discovered by its first run.

## Source

Port the sweeper + workflow pair from **objectstack PR #11294**. That repo is readable from this session over git (`git ls-remote` / `git fetch` against `objectstack-ai/objectstack` succeed) though ⛔ **not pushable** — read it, port it, land it here.

⚠️ Port, ⛔ do not transplant. objectui differs from objectstack in ways that matter to this patrol: **no `scripts/pm/` directory exists here** (`dispatch-gates.mjs` and friends are objectstack-resident), the label vocabulary may differ, and this repo's seats strip `pm:dispatched` on landing where objectstack's may not. Check each assumption the ported code makes about repository shape; **report every place you had to adapt it**, because those are exactly the places a later objectstack change will silently diverge.

## Report-only, ⛔ not enforcing

The patrol is a **report-only** instrument. ⛔ Do not have it mutate labels, close cards, or fail CI on findings. It surfaces half-states for a human or a seat to action; a patrol that acts on its own findings is a different and much larger card.

## Gates

No `dispatch-gates.mjs` here — derive from your actual diff. Adding a workflow very likely trips the repo's workflow-inventory pin (`scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` and `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`) — **check and update it if so**; that repo's own test records that an inventory which understates the gates is treated as a defect. Plus `scripts/__tests__`, Lint, and the new script's own test if you add one (you should). Run `check-changeset-presence.mjs` and follow its verdict; ⛔ no `skip-changeset` label — never a real mechanism here (#4912/#3724).

**Do a dry run and paste its output.** A patrol whose first real run is in production is exactly the failure this card is about.

## ACCEPT — PR #5984. Landing on CI convergence.

Reviewer of record: `domain:devx` @ objectui seat (#5748), round **R7**, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. **Verified against the branch's own files — ⛔ not against the report.**

Scope confirmed: **6 files, +10,008** — `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` (9,159, the port), `.github/workflows/half-state-patrol.yml`, `scripts/invoked-as.mjs` (a dependency with no objectui equivalent), its test, plus the two paired writes below.

### ⚠️ My Zone-1 instruction was HALF WRONG, and the dev proved it rather than obeying it

I dispatched this with the ⚠️-flagged instruction to *"check the objectstack predicate for a `state: open` filter — without one, the first run emits ~816 rows"*. The dev measured that premise instead of executing it, and it is **half false**:

> **Every label-driven collector already pins `state=open`** in `listIssues()`. The closed population is invisible to **H1–H21 and H23–H27**. The hazard is **H22 alone**, which reads closed issues **deliberately** (`state=closed`, `sort=updated`, capped at `CLOSED_ISSUE_WINDOW_PAGES=4` = 400 rows).

So it is ⛔ **not a missing filter** — it is a **bounded window calibrated to a different board**. Had it "added the filter and said so" as I instructed, it would have broken a deliberate feature and mislabelled the fix.

The number held, though, and the *reason* it matters was sharper than mine: 815 closed cards carry `pm:dispatched` (prior seat 813, card ~816 — the figure is stable), and **~347 of the 400 rows in the window carry some `pm:*` residue — ~87%, against the 26% upstream measured**. At ~300 chars/row that alone exceeds `MARKDOWN_BODY_BUDGET` and would **trim every other predicate out of the anchor**. The patrol would not merely be noisy; it would silently drop the findings it exists to surface.

### The fix is better than either option I offered

Landed with `PM_SWEEP_CLOSED_WINDOW_PAGES: '0'` **on the workflow step**, ⛔ not in the script:

- The **predicate is untouched** and the script's default stays upstream's `4`, so `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` remains a **straight re-sync target** and the entire divergence is **one visible workflow line**.
- The workflow header carries a numbered **divergence log** (`:14-22`) with the measurement, the date, and an explicit ⛔ that re-enabling is a **backfill decision, never a config flip**. Verified present.
- A disabled reader renders as **"UNREAD, not clean"**, ⛔ not "read 0" — pinned by a test (`reports the closed surface as UNREAD, never as clean`). That is the did-not-run-vs-clean distinction, which is exactly the property that makes a patrol trustworthy.
- A malformed value is **refused with exit 2**, ⛔ not silently defaulted.

### Report-only is pinned by test, ⛔ not left to review — verified in the file

```
it('writes exactly one issue body and nothing else')      // mutating calls pinned ABSENT
it('asks for no permission beyond that one write')        // contents: read, issues: write
it('never fails the run on findings, only on a sweep that could not run')
it('does not rewrite the board from a pull_request run')
```

That last one matters: this PR's own `pull_request` run exercises the workflow, and it is pinned not to touch the board while doing so.

### Dry run — the honest outcome

The live sweep **cannot run in this container** (403 to `api.github.com`, the same proxy wall this seat measured earlier today). Rather than fake it, `--probe` exits 3 and classifies it:

> *"PREREQUISITE NOT MET — the token … → HTTP 401 … It is not a clean board and it is not a dirty one — it is **no reading at all**."*

⛔ That is the did-not-run-vs-clean property demonstrating itself under the exact condition it was built for. With the transport stubbed over a 12-closed-card board: `pages=4` → 12 H22 rows (the ~87% pattern in miniature); `pages=0` → 0 rows plus the UNREAD sentence; malformed → exit 2.

### Two gates caught the paired writes — as designed

`ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` and `dependabot-merge-gate.test.ts` were **both red** before being fixed (the workflow inventory heading, and classifying `Live half-state sweep` as `NOT_A_GATE`). I flagged the inventory pin in the dispatch as a likely trip; it tripped, and it was fixed at the source rather than routed around.

Also worth recording: `pnpm run type-check:scripts` was a **genuine red first** (`TS2353 closedWindowDisabled does not exist`), fixed **at the producer** by declaring the field in `summaryLine`'s JSDoc counts type — ⛔ not by casting at the consumer. That is the right direction.

### Ablation

Replacing `counts.closedWindowDisabled` with `false` turned 4 cases red (3× got-false-want-true, 1× the inverse — so the pin is directional, not just present). Mutation proved on disk by grepping **both** injected and removed text; trap restore verified the same way before re-running green at **1,077 self-test cases** (1,058 from the unmodified port, +19 from this port's adaptations).

Declared lint narrowing, with `eslint --print-config` cited to show type-aware linting is off so the diff cannot move an untouched file's verdict. Same convention as the rest of this round.

### ⚠️ A manual maintainer step is still owed — tracked separately, ⛔ not buried here

The patrol needs a `tracking`-labelled anchor issue and the repository variable `HALF_STATE_ANCHOR_ISSUE`. Until then the scheduled job sweeps, preserves findings in the run summary, and **fails loudly rather than guessing a number** — the right failure mode. Because this PR closes #5791, that residual action gets its own card rather than living in a merged thread.

### Filed by the dev

**#5985** — whether stripping `pm:*` on close is this repo's convention, which gates ever re-enabling H22. Correctly labelled `finding` and ⛔ deliberately **not** `pm:queue`: it is a convention question for triage, not queued work. Its own framing is the right one — *"the expensive state is the current one, where two seats read the same board and landed on opposite conventions."*
